title: The Discovery of Oz, the Terrible, part 2
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: The four travelers passed a sleepless night, each thinking of the gift Oz had promised to bestow on him. Dorothy fell asleep only once, and then she dreamed she was in Kansas, where Aunt Em was telling her how glad she was to have her little girl at home again.
Promptly at nine o’clock the next morning the green-whiskered soldier came to them, and four minutes later they all went into the Throne Room of the Great Oz.

Of course each one of them expected to see the Wizard in the shape he had taken before, and all were greatly surprised when they looked about and saw no one at all in the room. They kept close to the door and closer to one another, for the stillness of the empty room was more dreadful than any of the forms they had seen Oz take.
Presently they heard a solemn Voice, that seemed to come from somewhere near the top of the great dome, and it said:
“I am Oz, the Great and Terrible. Why do you seek me?”
They looked again in every part of the room, and then, seeing no one, Dorothy asked, “Where are you?”

“I am everywhere,” answered the Voice, “but to the eyes of common mortals I am invisible. I will now seat myself upon my throne, that you may converse with me.” Indeed, the Voice seemed just then to come straight from the throne itself; so they walked toward it and stood in a row while Dorothy said:
“We have come to claim our promise, O Oz.”
“You promised to send me back to Kansas when the Wicked Witch was destroyed,” said the girl.
“And you promised to give me brains,” said the Scarecrow.
“And you promised to give me a heart,” said the Tin Woodman.
“And you promised to give me courage,” said the Cowardly Lion.
“Is the Wicked Witch really destroyed?” asked the Voice, and Dorothy thought it trembled a little.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Dorothy dream?
options: That she was in Kansas with Aunt Em
That the Wizard had refused them
That the Witch had come back to life
That the Monkeys carried her home

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did they find in the Throne Room?
options: No one at all
The great Head on the throne
The lovely Lady waiting
A Ball of Fire burning

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where did the Voice seem to come from?
options: Near the top of the great dome
Behind the screen in the corner
From under the green marble throne
From outside the closed door

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Voice say about being seen?
options: That to common mortals he is invisible
That he had gone away for a time
That only Dorothy could see him
That the spectacles hid him

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Dorothy say they had come for?
options: To claim their promise
To ask for another favour
To report the Witch's death only
To say goodbye to the city

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why was the empty room so dreadful to them?
options: The stillness was worse than any shape Oz had taken
They feared the Wizard had already gone
They thought the Monkeys had destroyed him
The room was darker than it had been before

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what did Dorothy notice in the Voice's last question?
options: That it seemed to tremble a little
That it came from a different place
That it had grown much louder
That it spoke in a woman's tone

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how did the four spend the night before?
options: Sleepless, each thinking of his promised gift
Soundly asleep after their long journey
Arguing about what to ask the Wizard
Preparing to leave the city at dawn

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does converse with me mean?
options: Talk with me
Argue with me
Travel with me
Bargain with me

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: An audience with a Wizard who cannot be seen, and four claims made
An audience in which the Wizard grants every wish at once
A discovery that the Throne Room has been abandoned
A quarrel between the four about who should speak first

questions.prompt: According to the passage, at what hour did the soldier come for them?
options: Promptly at nine o'clock
Four minutes after nine
At sunrise that morning
At noon exactly

questions.prompt: Per the passage, where did the Voice say it would seat itself?
options: Upon the throne
Behind the corner screen
At the top of the dome
Beside the little door

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what had Aunt Em said in the dream?
options: How glad she was to have her little girl home
That Dorothy must never leave the farm again
That the house had been rebuilt at last
That Uncle Henry had gone to look for her

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how did the four behave in the empty room?
options: Kept close to the door and close to one another
Spread out to search every corner at once
Sat down on the floor to wait
Called out for the Wizard by name

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what had each of them expected to see?
options: The shape Oz had taken for him before
The little old man behind the screen
An empty room with nobody in it
All four shapes of Oz at once

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does solemn describe about the Voice?
options: Grave and serious in tone
Loud enough to shake the dome
Kindly and welcoming
Weak and hard to hear

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: Four promises are claimed from a voice with no body to be seen
Four travellers find the Throne Room empty and leave again
The Wizard appears in a fifth shape none of them expected
Dorothy alone is admitted while the others wait outside
